tasks.title: Make a nested git repository its own vloop root (C-2) and have verify make its scratches repositories
tasks.goal: B18's and B19's verify sessions built scratch repositories under .vloop/tmp/ that resolved to this repository's .vloop/, so their `vloop config set` edited the real config and no verify report was written. C-2 changes so the root is the nearest ancestor holding .vloop/ or .git, whichever is found first, level by level; a directory under a vloop repository with no nearer .git or .vloop/ still resolves to the vloop repository. The verify skill then makes every scratch in which an example runs vloop or git a repository with git init, so nothing it runs reaches this repository.

references.why: Root is the one place the root is resolved; it searches each marker over all ancestors in turn today, which is why an outer .vloop/ beats a nearer .git
TestRootNearestVloopWinsOverGit pins today's C-2 for exactly the nested case whose answer changes; it is the only earlier test this task may change, and only to the new answer
C-2 under "Configuration — C" is rewritten in the brief's exact words; no other invariant changes
"The repo root" states C-2's rule in prose and must say the same as the new C-2
"## 2. Build into a scratch directory" is where the scratch-is-a-repository rule goes, citing C-2; the skill has a word ceiling in internal/budget the go check enforces

acceptance: config.Root returns, for a start directory, the nearest ancestor (the start directory included) that holds .vloop or .git, checking both at each level before moving up; else the start directory
A .git file (a worktree or a submodule) counts as .git
Violation, ruled against: a root that skips a nearer .git to reach an outer .vloop/; or one that stops at a nearer .git when the start directory itself holds .vloop/

In a vloop repository, `(cd .vloop/tmp/w && vloop config set language es)` with .vloop/tmp/w a git repository exits 0, writes .vloop/tmp/w/.vloop/config.toml with language = "es", and leaves the outer .vloop/config.toml unchanged
In the same repository, `(cd .vloop/tmp/plain && vloop config get language)` with no .git in .vloop/tmp/plain prints en, the outer repository's value

docs/domain/domain-model.md's C-2 reads: The repo root is the nearest ancestor (the start directory included) holding `.vloop/` or `.git`, whichever is found first; else the start directory. Every path vloop prints is relative to it, with `/`.
docs/domain/platform/platform-context.md's "The repo root" says the same rule in prose and no longer says ".vloop/, else .git"

plugin/skills/verify/SKILL.md's "Build into a scratch directory" says a scratch directory in which an example runs vloop or git is made a repository first (git init), so it is its own root (C-2) and nothing it runs reaches this repository

internal/config/root_test.go's nested case is changed to the new answer (a nearer .git wins over an outer .vloop/) and nothing else in it is weakened; the work notes name C-2 as the contract item for that change

The task leaves committed tests the go check runs in internal/config: a nested .git under an outer .vloop/, a .git file, a start directory holding .vloop/ under an outer .git, both markers in one directory, and a directory with neither under a vloop repository; on Windows-shaped paths where the code handles one

tasks.title: Treat a brief's bare name, .loop-brief name and path as one brief, and write the .loop-brief name
tasks.goal: Interventions recorded with a bare brief name vanish from `vloop metrics`, which counts only records whose brief: field is the .loop-brief name. Every command that takes a brief — metrics, defect and intervention add and list, and intervention set brief — must accept the bare name, the .loop-brief name and a path whose base name is <name>.loop-brief.md as one brief; records are always written with the .loop-brief name, and list and metrics match a record written with either the bare or the .loop-brief name so old records count. No record schema or metrics formula changes, and nothing rewrites existing records.

references.why: BriefName and CheckBrief normalise and check a brief today and List matches on it; the fix of the brief-name match belongs here, and a name that is not a loop brief must still be refused as today
add, set brief and List by brief use defect.BriefName and the same exact match; they must write the .loop-brief name and match both forms
Build gathers a brief's defects and interventions through defect.List and intervention.List; it must count bare-name records without any formula changing
M-1: metrics are keyed by brief; M-4: the recorded defects that must count whatever name their brief: field carries

acceptance: `vloop metrics`, `vloop defect list --brief`, `vloop intervention list --brief`, `vloop defect add --brief` and `vloop intervention add --brief` accept B20261022-1234-x, B20261022-1234-x.loop-brief and docs/briefs/B20261022-1234-x.loop-brief.md (any path whose base name is <name>.loop-brief.md) as the same brief
`defect add`, `intervention add` and `intervention set <id> brief <value>` write brief: <name>.loop-brief whichever form they were given
Violation, ruled against: a record written with a bare or a path brief name

list and metrics match a record whose brief: field is either the bare or the .loop-brief name; on this repository, `vloop metrics` of B20261002-2135-vloop-v1-security in the three forms gives equal "defects" and "interventions"
A name that is not a loop brief (for example a .architect-brief.md) or a loop brief that does not exist is refused by defect add as today, writing nothing
No record schema, metrics formula or existing record changes; no command renames or rewrites existing records' brief names

The task leaves committed tests the go check runs: the three forms resolving to one brief, add writing the .loop-brief name, and a planted bare-name defect and intervention counted by list and by the metrics

tasks.title: Mask the system temp directory as $TMPDIR in everything the driver masks (#53)
tasks.goal: A plan session's record kept the machine's temp directory (the per-user temp folder on macOS), which is machine-specific and breaks the no-absolute-paths rule (issue #53, defect D20261024-162448). Mask must replace the system temp directory — os.TempDir() and, where it is a symbolic link, its resolved form — with $TMPDIR wherever it masks the home directory today: session records, stderr files, the run log. It runs after the home masking, so a temp directory under the home still comes out as ~/…, and a temp directory of /tmp or /var/tmp is left alone, because briefs and gates name those. No other directory (GOCACHE, XDG_*, caches) is masked.

references.why: Mask, redactSecrets and homePattern: the temp directory joins the home here, matched at path boundaries and in JSON-escaped and Windows-shaped forms the way the home is
M-7: no absolute paths in an export, which records carrying the temp directory break

acceptance: With TMPDIR a symbolic link, a plan session denied `rm -rf <TMPDIR>/x.1` and `rm -rf <resolved TMPDIR>/y.2` is recorded in sessions/001-plan.json as `rm -rf $TMPDIR/x.1` and `rm -rf $TMPDIR/y.2`, and neither form of the temp directory occurs anywhere in the run folder (session records, stderr files, the run log)
The temp directory is masked after the home: with TMPDIR under HOME, a denial of <TMPDIR>/x.1 is recorded as ~/tmp/x.1 (for TMPDIR = HOME/tmp)
Violation, ruled against: /tmp or /var/tmp rewritten to $TMPDIR — with TMPDIR=/tmp a denial of /tmp/x.1 is kept as /tmp/x.1
Nothing else is newly masked: no GOCACHE, XDG_* or cache path

The task leaves committed tests the go check runs in internal/driver: the temp directory and its resolved form masked, /tmp and /var/tmp kept, a temp directory under the home giving ~/…, and a Windows-shaped temp directory where the code handles one

tasks.title: Check that a GitHub login reaches Copilot sessions in doctor and the run preflight, and reword the experimental warning
tasks.goal: B19's acceptance found that a Copilot session's own COPILOT_HOME holds no login, so it falls back to the environment and `gh auth token`; an interactive /login does not reach vloop's sessions, and a run only found out after a failed review session. With agent.review = copilot, doctor gains a copilot login row and `vloop run` refuses before planning when neither COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN (set and not empty) nor `gh auth token` (exit 0, prints something) provides a login; the token is never printed, logged or kept. The experimental warning stops naming B20, and the guide says how a session logs in. Take gh's and Copilot's behaviour from their docs or from running them, never from memory (the repository's guidelines); no test runs the real copilot, gh or the network.

references.why: the Copilot adapter's Preflight, which the login check extends; its sessions' environment is what the login must reach

doctorCopilot and copilotExperimental: the copilot login row goes beside the copilot checks, shown only when agent.review is copilot, and the warning text changes here; runPreflight in internal/cli/run.go reads these rows
the Copilot paragraph, which says "experimental until B20" today and must say "experimental until the fence lands" and how a Copilot session logs in

acceptance: With agent.review = copilot and no login, `vloop doctor` prints `✗ copilot login no GitHub login reaches Copilot sessions: set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, or run gh auth login` and exits 1; with a login it prints `✓ copilot login`
A login is COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN set and not empty, or `gh auth token` exiting 0 and printing something; an empty variable or a gh that prints nothing is not a login

With agent.review = copilot and no login, `vloop run <brief>` exits 1 before planning, starting no session, with `vloop: agent.review is copilot but no GitHub login reaches its sessions: set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, or run gh auth login` on stderr
With agent.review = claude, doctor shows no copilot login row and runs no login check
Violation, ruled against: a token printed, logged or kept in any record, file or message — including in an error that quotes gh's output

The warning in doctor and the run preflight reads `! agent.review is copilot: experimental — review sessions are not fenced yet (docs/guide/configuration.md)`; violation, ruled against: the old "not fenced until B20" text left anywhere a session or the operator reads it (code, tests, plugin, guide)

docs/guide/configuration.md's Copilot paragraph says "experimental until the fence lands" and that a Copilot session logs in through COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, else gh (`gh auth login`)
The earlier tests change only where they pin the old warning text, and only to the new text; the work notes name R4's warning as the contract item for that change

The task leaves committed tests the go check runs in internal/cli: the copilot login row ✓ and ✗ for each source (each variable, an empty variable, a gh stub that prints a token, exits 1 or prints nothing), the run preflight's refusal, no row with agent.review = claude, and the token absent from the output; the tests are hermetic — a stub gh on PATH and the token variables unset, so a real login on the machine cannot pass them
